goods.name: Moon pebble
goods.blurb: A smooth grey pebble off Slate's one beach, polished by a moon with no weather. Otters give them to each other and mean it.

goods.name: Hedgerow grain
goods.blurb: Sacks of Moss barley, still smelling of hedgerow. Cats will pay for anything that did not come out of a tube.

goods.name: Bond-paper & ink
goods.blurb: Moss-pressed paper and squid ink. The Emberkin write everything down and are always out of both.

goods.name: Ship fittings
goods.blurb: Crates of Slate-made valves, seals and struts. Far from any dry dock, cats keep ships flying with these and oaths.

goods.name: Kelp rope & sailcloth
goods.blurb: Tassel harbour cordage. Every port in the system tethers something with it.

goods.name: Belt ore
goods.blurb: Nickel-iron chipped off belt rocks. The engine smiths of Cinder melt it into things that go very fast.

goods.name: Ring ice
goods.blurb: Blocks of clean outer-system ice. Parched Cinder pays for every drop; the frogs cannot imagine why.

goods.name: Ember-salt
goods.blurb: Yellow sulfur salts raked from Cinder's dayside. Fertilizer for Moss, heater chemistry for the frogs.

goods.name: Hedgerow fruit
goods.blurb: Plums, pears and hedge-berries. Nothing tastes better in microgravity, and nothing rots faster.

goods.name: Tidepool oysters
goods.blurb: Packed in wet kelp. Twenty days of shelf life if you are lucky, and cats are never lucky enough.

goods.name: Ember fashions
goods.blurb: This week's Veyra look, folded in heat-paper. Worth a fortune fresh and an embarrassment in three months.

goods.name: Tideglass lanterns
goods.blurb: Otter glasswork that glows sea-green in the dark. The frogs hang them under the lily-pads and sing to them.

goods.name: Ember filigree
goods.blurb: Brass and obsidian filigree forged in a week and treasured for a lifetime, which for the maker is about the same thing.

goods.name: Song-shells
goods.blurb: Resonant shells that hold a frog song for centuries. Tassel plays them at parties; Cinder scholars transcribe them.

goods.name: Whisker shadow-silk
goods.blurb: Spun on Whisker from something nobody there will name. Drinks light, and arrives without paperwork.

goods.name: Maw dust
goods.blurb: Glittering grit swept off the ring the Maw wears. Fireworks on Cinder, wedding confetti on Tassel, and dear because of where it comes from.

goods.name: Haven ice-wine
goods.blurb: Fermented under ammonia ice over a frog lifetime. Boils into vinegar above freezing, so keep it cold.

goods.name: Cold cultures
goods.blurb: Living medicinal cultures from the lily-pad apothecaries. Otter healers swear by them; warmth kills them.

goods.name: Builder tube-segment
goods.blurb: A length of seamless Builder tube cut from the Arc. Hums when you tap it. Nobody knows what it was for.

goods.name: Ringing glass
goods.blurb: Glass snow off the shell of Glass, still faintly ringing the note the Builders left in it.

goods.name: Dampener shard
goods.blurb: A splinter of Builder dampener, kept by the Croak ascetics. Sound dies within a hand of it. The engine smiths want it very badly.

goods.name: Otter travelers
goods.blurb: Cousins visiting cousins. They will talk the whole way and know everyone at the other end.

goods.name: Emberkin travelers
goods.blurb: In heated suits, tapping their feet. They pay most for speed and remind you of the deadline hourly.

goods.name: Cat crew on leave
goods.blurb: Lanky, bored, and full of opinions about your approach vector. Never carry them to a heavy world.

goods.name: Frog pilgrims
goods.blurb: Bound for Haven to walk in the festival. They need the hold kept cold and will hum the entire way.

cinder.name: Cinder
cinder.notes: Engine smiths; the cheapest fuel in the system straight from the refineries.

scorch.name: Scorch
scorch.notes: Mining frontier. Cheap rock, dangerous work, and the Emberkin nobody at home writes to.

veyra.name: Veyra
veyra.notes: Auction houses and money. Everything is for sale and everybody is watching who buys it.

tassel.name: Tassel
tassel.notes: The gossip hub and starting port. Big market, honest prices, terrible secrets.

slate.name: Slate
slate.notes: Dry docks and cranes. Tanks, holds and refrigeration are fitted here, with commentary.

moss.name: Moss
moss.notes: Farming moon, green to the shoreline. Will sell you grain and fruit and ask where you bank.

nail.name: Nail
nail.notes: Belt haven. Repairs, salvage and a bar. Match speeds and knock.

whisker.name: Whisker
whisker.notes: The shady end of the Belt. No questions, no paperwork, and a fitter who works in the dark.

arc.name: The Arc
arc.notes: Cat salvagers camped on the rim of a Builder ring, riding just beyond the Belt. No fuel; bring your own or beg.

grumm.name: Grumm
grumm.notes: Balloon cities in the cold upper clouds. The trade window for the whole frog system.

brine.name: Brine
brine.notes: Ammonia seas and floating apothecaries. Chemistry nobody else can read.

glass.name: Glass
glass.notes: Research station over an ocean under ice. They study the Builders and will talk your ear off.

croak.name: Croak
croak.notes: Retrograde and austere. Barely a market. The approach is dear on purpose.

haven.name: Haven
haven.notes: The frog capital and the outer system’s great market. No haggling; prices are exchange rates and goodwill.

maw.name: The Maw
maw.notes: No market. Something down there is still keeping station.

upgrades.name: Slack tank
upgrades.unlocks: Tassel's moons and the slow road out to the Belt with a refuel.

upgrades.name: Long-haul tank
upgrades.unlocks: A comfortable transfer to the Belt and the Arc; Grumm with careful routing.

upgrades.name: Deep-sky tank
upgrades.unlocks: Direct Grumm runs, the Maw, and running hot with perishables.

upgrades.name: Slate putter
upgrades.effect: Starter fuel efficiency: km/s bought per cowrie at the pump (factor from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing; it is what you came with.

upgrades.name: Cinder fastburn
upgrades.effect: Better fuel efficiency: more km/s per cowrie when refuelling (factor from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Cheaper hot transfers; the Cinder run stops eating your margin.

upgrades.name: Smiths' masterwork
upgrades.unlocks: Outer-system fuel prices stop mattering as much.

upgrades.name: Starter hold
upgrades.effect: Starter cargo capacity (units from tuning; the sim assumes 24).
upgrades.unlocks: Nothing; it is what you came with.

upgrades.name: Raft hold
upgrades.unlocks: Bulk runs that actually pay; two passenger cabins plus cargo.

upgrades.name: Barge hold
upgrades.unlocks: Relic hauls and full frog gift-exchanges in one trip.

upgrades.name: Ember heat shield
upgrades.effect: Survive atmosphere skims; enables aerobraking at Grumm.
upgrades.unlocks: Free braking at Grumm ("Skimming"); the fast cheap road to Haven.

upgrades.name: Cold hold
upgrades.effect: Hold can carry goods and passengers flagged needsRefrigeration.
upgrades.unlocks: Ice-wine, cold cultures and frog pilgrims.

upgrades.name: Long-range sensors
upgrades.effect: Shows Arc salvage sites and Belt traffic on the chart with intercept predictions.
upgrades.unlocks: Salvage contracts, quiet Belt work, and the long look outward.

upgrades.name: Whisker dampener
upgrades.effect: Cat toll intercepts in the Belt no longer trigger unless you dock at Nail.

price.description: You pay base*sells.priceMul*(1-repDiscount)*haggle. A port pays base*demandBy[species]*buys.priceMul*alignment*saturation*perishable*haggle*(1+volatility wobble). A port with no people of its own uses the mean of the four species demands.

alignment.description: For a good at buyer port B, d = current distance to the good's nearest producer port A. With dmin/dmax the geometric min/max separation of the two orbits (capped at maxSeparationAu), x = clamp((d-dmin)/(dmax-dmin),0,1); mul = clamp(1 + k*(x-0.5), minMul, maxMul). Same-parent pairs (dmax-dmin < 0.05 au) get mul 1. Close worlds flood the market, far worlds go hungry.

saturation.description: Each port remembers recentSold[good] (items), decaying with half-life halfLifeDays. The k-th item you sell fetches q0eff/(q0eff+recentSold) of the price, q0eff = q0*port.marketSize, updated after every item.

perishable.description: Perishable value multiplier = floor + (1-floor)*max(0, 1 - ageDays/lifetimeDays); linear decay to the floor, shown in the UI as "loses X% per day".

reputation.description: Reputation is 0..10 points per species. Purchases and fuel at that species' ports are discounted by min(maxDiscount, discountPerPoint*points). Frog gifts scale with frog reputation; cat tolls fall by the same fraction.

toll.description: A Belt toll intercept takes min(cap, fraction*cargoValue) in goods, chosen by the cats; nothing if cargoValue < minCargoValue (they never take everything, never touch passengers, and never harm a ship that yields). Stealth suppresses intercepts.

tow.description: A stranded or crashed ship is towed to the nearest port: cost = base + perAu*distanceAu, time = max(3, daysPerAu*distanceAu) days. If you cannot pay, the Tassel harbour bank fronts it and the debt is deducted from sales.

contract.description: Pay = basePerAu*max(minAu, separationAu)*deadlineDays[tightness]*speciesMul[species]*template.payMul per passenger or cargo lot, plus the boarding fee; deadline = tightnessOverHohmann[tightness]*HohmannDays; earlyBonus fraction extra if delivered within half the deadline.

haggle.description: Otter ports: each visit rolls a uniform spread of +-spread on every price, then a haggle mini-exchange lets you keep the good end of the roll. Frogs never haggle (spread 0). Cats and Emberkin do not haggle either.

volatility.description: Daily random-walk wobble on what a port pays, amplitude by species. Emberkin markets are the most volatile.

speciesRules.otter: Haggle spread on every price; refusing to haggle is rude (small rep loss).
speciesRules.emberkin: Volatile prices; perishable fashions; contracts pay the most for speed (speciesMul 1.3, earlyBonus counts double).
speciesRules.cat: Tolls in the Belt under strict custom (never everything, never passengers). Impress a captain and a gift may follow.
speciesRules.frog: No haggling. "Prices" are exchange rates: you are paid in trade credit at the stall plus goodwill (reputation), and every visit ends with a gift.

templates.text: A crate of this season's fashions. Next season starts in a month. Fly.
An Emberkin apprentice with a letter of introduction to the Slate shipwrights and no patience whatsoever.
An elderly scholar (she is four) wants to see the Builder halls under Glass before she dies of old age.
Cousins, a wedding, and a cake that must not be tilted.
Relief caretakers for the Scorch camps, plus three months of gossip in written form.
An otter banker with a sealed case wants to be at Nail before the salvage auction closes. Do not ask.
A load of Moss fruit for the Nail tavern. It pays by the crate that arrives edible.
A crew on leave, bound for the tavern. They will critique every burn.
A salvage lot from a marked Arc site, to be delivered to a buyer who will pretend not to know what it is.
A parcel for the quiet end of the Belt. Do not look inside and do not be late.
Pilgrims for Croak. Keep the hold cold and do not hurry them.
A song-keeper who has waited ninety years for a ride to Glass and can wait a little longer, in the cold.
A crate of cold cultures for the Tassel healers, given freely; the healers will pay you.
A belt family heading in-system. They know a route you do not.

sim.notes: orbitAu per port is the circular radius used for straight-line distance and Hohmann estimates; moons quote their parent’s radius.
